source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS02 is a 114 MW IT capacity campus in Sterling, Virginia, the third largest of the 25 Virginia data centers that publish a megawatt figure.

That ranking is the useful part. Virginia has 330 mapped data centers, but only 25 disclose capacity, and those 25 total 1,603 MW. One facility therefore accounts for 7.1 percent of all published state IT load. The published total is a floor, not a measurement, because the other 305 facilities are unmapped on this dimension. Any claim about Virginia's true data center capacity has to start by admitting that most of it is undisclosed.

For AI specifically, 114 MW is the number that matters. At a common assumption of 400 watts per rack for training workloads, that is roughly 285 racks, or about 2,280 high-end accelerators at 8 GPUs per rack. The 685,000 square feet of technical space and the LEED certification describe the building, but the megawatt figure is what bounds the compute. A campus this size is material for training or serving at scale, and it sits in Ashburn, inside Northern Virginia's existing power and network backbone, 3.5 miles from Dulles.

What the data does not say is whether that power can be expanded. Grid constraints, interconnection queues, and available headroom in the region are not published here. The facility's capacity is known. The ceiling above it is not.
